kvcache.title: KV Cache Technology Evaluation Multi-Agent
kvcache.description: An Agentic RAG that writes technology evaluation reports, redesigned as multi-agent

detail.overview: The system evaluates KIVI (2-bit KV quantization, software) and ITME (CXL memory expansion, hardware) by technology readiness, market, stakeholders and domain, and generates a citation-checked PDF report. Built first as a fixed-order graph in the RAG Pipeline module, then converted into a multi-agent design where a Supervisor assigns work dynamically in the AI Agent module.
tasks: Designed the web search node and the shared per-perspective subgraph; owned graph wiring and verification
Normalized the evidence-sufficiency judge, made it fail closed, and added a single refinement loop
Ran a 30-question retrieval evaluation to compare embedding models (BGE-M3 Hit@5 0.800 vs multilingual-e5-large 0.700)
Designed Supervisor routing, per-task parallel dispatch (Send), the State schema and reducers
Separated control state from data state; guaranteed termination with layered caps and fallbacks
Parallelized judging: test run 372.8s → 240.2s (−35.6%)

gonggong.title: Gonggong Chwippo: Listed-Company Cross-Check Agent
gonggong.description: An agent that cross-checks disclosures, financials, jobs and news for per-company checkpoints

detail.overview: The service cross-checks a listed company's disclosures (OpenDART), Financial Services Commission data, National Pension employment data and news to surface points that a company profile alone doesn't show. Classification runs on GPT-4o-mini and analysis on GPT-4o, with a human-in-the-loop approval step before saving results.
tasks: Assembled the agent flow and defined how tools connect (integration contract)
Implemented cross-source verification logic
Built fixture-based offline tests that reproduce results without external APIs

solarcast.title: SolarCast: Solar Power Forecasting AIOps
solarcast.description: An MLOps pipeline that detects drift and decides on retraining, promotion and rollback

detail.overview: An LSTM model trained on 762 days of Korea Power Exchange (KPX) public data forecasts solar generation and is served with FastAPI, with versions managed by an MLflow model registry and a deployment gate. When forecast error (WAPE) exceeds 0.388, the pipeline treats it as drift, retrains, and promotes the new model only if it passes the gate.
tasks: Redesigned the class example (stock prediction) for the solar domain; preprocessed KPX data
Set up the MLflow deployment gate and model registry
Verified drift detection: WAPE 0.179 on a normal batch vs 0.460 on a drifted batch
Verified retraining decisions: spring-data model rejected; recovery-period model promoted to v2 (RMSE 7,716), then rolled back to v1
Compared model loading: first response 2.560s (lazy) → 0.642s (eager)

Order summary API (pair work): authorization inside the query and a fallback message when the model call fails

thesis.title: Sparse Point Cloud Completion (Master's Thesis)
thesis.description: A 3D completion framework that keeps shapes intact on sparse input

detail.overview: Transformer-based completion models such as SeedFormer learn only to minimize coordinate distance, so sharp edges and boundaries collapse when input is sparse. Without major architecture changes, I added two modules that teach geometry explicitly. (A Transformer-based Framework for Sparse Point Cloud Completion with Geometric Constraints)
tasks: Distribution-Matching Loss (DML): aligns local point density with ground truth to stop points from clustering
Hole Uncertainty Weighting (HUW): finds empty regions of the input and raises their training weight
Compared against GRNet, SnowflakeNet and SeedFormer at 1,024 / 512 / 256 input points
Ablation: DML alone 22.10, HUW alone 21.50, both 19.20, showing the modules are complementary

anomaly.title: Semiconductor Process Anomaly Detection & Yield Root Cause
anomaly.description: Found the 93%-accuracy trap and redesigned evaluation first
anomaly.role: Analysis design, modeling and report automation
features: 13 latent defects found · top 10 yield variables

detail.overview: The SECOM process sensor data (1,567 samples, 590 sensors) has only 6.6% defects, a 14:1 imbalance where predicting 'normal' for everything already scores 93% accuracy. I rebuilt the evaluation around the manufacturing view that missing a defect is worse than a false alarm.
tasks: Cleaned missing and zero-variance features (466 of 590 kept); SMOTE oversampled training defects from 83 to 1,170
XGBoost + Isolation Forest ensemble, 405 GridSearchCV combinations, threshold tuned from 0.5 to 0.25
Mean sensor deviation 2.14 for detected vs 0.10 for missed defects: a data limit, not a tuning problem
Follow-up: XGBoost yield model (ROC-AUC 0.696) + SHAP on 104 defects (top variable F59, SHAP 0.400)
Built a single pipeline from preprocessing to modeling, prediction and PDF reporting

trademark.title: AI Trademark Registrability Assessment
trademark.description: An assessment model that follows an examiner's reasoning order
trademark.role: Criteria structuring, prompt design and model validation

detail.overview: Trademark examination is long and varies by examiner, making registrability hard to predict before filing. I structured KIPO examination guidelines and case law by decision factor, and designed step-by-step prompts that judge in the order generic term → customary mark → distinctiveness.
tasks: Structured examination guidelines and case law by decision factor
Converted legal text into model-ready input; designed few-shot templates
Cross-validated GPT-4o, GPT-3.5 Turbo and Llama
Categorized errors to find limits such as composite figurative marks → proposed an OCR-based multimodal extension

gs3d.title: 3DGS Alignment Error Root Cause
gs3d.description: Pinpointed a recurring alignment error with numbers
gs3d.role: Alignment error root cause analysis and issue tracking

detail.overview: When objects were trained separately for real-time rendering of game scenes with 3D Gaussian Splatting, an unexplained alignment error kept recurring. With each team blaming a different cause, I ran every possible combination and measured where the error appeared.
tasks: Controlled variables by applying ground-truth camera parameters and unifying dataset settings
Ran every simulation combination and quantified where and how large the error was
Aligned coordinate systems with Python matrix ops and the Umeyama transform; fixed the COLMAP normalization anchor
Proposed a compromise by comparing each team's fix on estimated effort and rendering efficiency

tcad.title: Optical Modulator Simulation Automation
tcad.description: Turned hundreds of device simulations into automatic run-and-compare
tcad.role: Undergraduate researcher · Advanced Semiconductor Devices Lab

detail.overview: Finding the best Mach-Zehnder modulator structure on Si photonics meant simulating hundreds of doping, thickness and strain conditions, each taking tens of minutes. I connected the two simulators with Python and compared results automatically.
tasks: Scripted Sentaurus TCAD (process and bias) and Lumerical MODE (optical modes)
Batch-simulated three structures (Si LPN / Si LSPN / SiGe LSPN) across bias voltages
Auto-extracted XML results → normalized loss and efficiency → compared by condition
Chose the best structure from Δneff vs voltage characteristics

torus.title: Torus Fitting Evaluation
torus.description: Approximated surfaces with torus patches and measured accuracy

detail.overview: I converted complex surfaces into voxel-based point clouds and fitted a torus patch to each local region. Beyond modeling, I built a frame that compares fitting accuracy numerically across settings.
tasks: Aligned patch orientation with PCA and curvature; computed fitting accuracy
Collected mean, variance and error rate for 54 settings
Analyzed which factors drive the result with a parameter correlation heatmap
